item.text: {"search_note":"I found strong evidence of program translation into budgets, councils, expert panels, laws, and oversight mechanisms.\nI did not find equally strong evidence of systematic appointment politics or a comprehensive, published implementation scorecard for every major priority in 2024.\nThe main negative evidence is about political damage, coalition compromise, and incomplete macro results, not about a lack of concrete plans.","evidence":[{"title":"Policy Speech by Prime Minister Kishida to the 213th Session of the Diet","publisher":"Prime Minister’s Office of Japan","date":"2024-01-30","url":"https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202401/30shiseihoshin.html","summary":"Kishida turned his program into a concrete agenda with named priorities: disaster response, wage growth, child support, fiscal reform, digital administration, labor-market reform, and defense/security buildup. This is direct evidence of translating program into priorities and a timetable for the year.","question_ids":["8B.1","8B.2"]},{"title":"New Year’s Reflection by Prime Minister KISHIDA Fumio","publisher":"Prime Minister’s Office of Japan","date":"2024-01-01","url":"https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202401/01nentou.html","summary":"He explicitly linked policy execution to political stability and public trust, showing a governing plan tied to implementation capacity, not just rhetoric.","question_ids":["8B.1","8B.2"]},{"title":"Prime Minister’s Office policy page: A New Form of Capitalism","publisher":"Prime Minister’s Office of Japan","date":"2024","url":"https://japan.kantei.go.jp/ongoingtopics/policies_kishida/newcapitalism.html","summary":"The official policy page packages the ideology into operational components: wage growth, human-capital investment, labor reform, redistribution, and middle-class expansion. This is the clearest institutionalized program statement.","question_ids":["8B.1","8B.2"]},{"title":"The 2024 revised New Form of Capitalism and Basic Economic Policy package","publisher":"Prime Minister’s Office of Japan","date":"2024-06-21","url":"https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/actions/202406/21keizai.html","summary":"Kishida moved the program into a formal economic policy package through councils and cabinet decisions, including broad subsidies and structural-growth policy. This is strong evidence of institutional translation, not just goals.","question_ids":["8B.2"]},{"title":"Budget guidelines for FY2025","publisher":"Prime Minister’s Office of Japan","date":"2024-07-29","url":"https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/actions/202407/29keizai.html","summary":"He approved budget guidelines built on medium- to long-term projections, private-demand-led growth, wage increases above inflation, and EBPM/“wise spending.” This directly shows program-to-budget translation.","question_ids":["8B.2"]},{"title":"Expert panel on active cyber defense","publisher":"Prime Minister’s Office of Japan","date":"2024-06-07","url":"https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/actions/202406/07cyber.html","summary":"Kishida convened a 17-expert panel to design legislation for active cyber defense. That is a concrete institutional mechanism for implementing the security side of his agenda.","question_ids":["8B.2"]},{"title":"Long-horizon energy and industrial strategy meeting","publisher":"Prime Minister’s Office of Japan","date":"2024-07-02","url":"https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/actions/202407/02gx_leaders.html","summary":"He brought business leaders and technical experts together with cabinet members to design long-horizon industrial and energy strategy. This is a direct implementation channel, not a vague promise.","question_ids":["8B.2"]},{"title":"Foreign-worker program reform meeting","publisher":"Prime Minister’s Office of Japan","date":"2024-02-09","url":"https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/actions/202402/09gaikoku.html","summary":"Kishida implemented expert-panel recommendations through ministers and bills, showing a formal pipeline from advice to legislation.","question_ids":["8B.2"]},{"title":"Nuclear Regulation Authority briefing on Shika restart screening","publisher":"Prime Minister’s Office of Japan","date":"2024-01-14","url":"https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202401/14kaiken.html","summary":"Kishida relied on expert regulatory screening and post-Fukushima standards for any restart, showing formal enforcement and safety oversight rather than ad hoc discretion.","question_ids":["8B.2"]},{"title":"Noto disaster response package","publisher":"Prime Minister’s Office of Japan","date":"2024-01-25","url":"https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202401/25kaiken.html","summary":"The government used cash aid, housing support, and service restoration for disaster victims, with specific attention to low-income households, schools, transit, SMEs, and agriculture. This is concrete budgeted delivery, not just an announced priority.","question_ids":["8B.2"]},{"title":"Reserve-fund recovery follow-up","publisher":"Prime Minister’s Office of Japan","date":"2024-07-01","url":"https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202407/01kaiken.html","summary":"Kishida reported multiple reserve-fund tranches restoring infrastructure, lifelines, housing, and livelihoods. This shows implementation through repeated budgetary disbursement and recovery administration.","question_ids":["8B.2"]},{"title":"AI provenance and trustworthy AI policy","publisher":"Prime Minister’s Office of Japan","date":"2024-05-02","url":"https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202405/02ai.html","summary":"Kishida translated concern about disinformation into a concrete governance agenda: safe, secure, trustworthy AI and provenance verification. This is a specific enforcement-oriented policy step.","question_ids":["8B.2"]},{"title":"JapanGov fact-checking / information-origin verification","publisher":"JapanGov / Government of Japan","date":"2024-01-26","url":"https://www.japan.go.jp/kizuna/2024/01/growing_importance_of_fact-checking.html","summary":"The government quoted Kishida saying information-origin verification technologies should be developed and diffused. This is a concrete implementation signal for the information-integrity part of the program.","question_ids":["8B.2"]},{"title":"August 14, 2024 LDP transition statement","publisher":"Prime Minister’s Office of Japan","date":"2024-08-14","url":"https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202408/14kaiken.html","summary":"Kishida said the LDP presidential race should be transparent and that he would step aside and support the winner chosen by vote. This shows a concrete timeline for succession and an internal rule-set for transfer of authority.","question_ids":["8B.2","8B.1"]},{"title":"Reuters: Kishida to step down amid scandals and living-cost anger","publisher":"Reuters","date":"2024-08-14","url":"https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/japan-pm-kishida-wont-run-for-reelection-at-ldp-race-kyodo-reports-3570455","summary":"Reuters framed the exit as driven by scandal and living costs, which suggests the program was politically constrained and not fully converted into durable governing leverage.","question_ids":["8B.2","8B.1"]},{"title":"Reuters: ethics committee and budget pressure","publisher":"Reuters","date":"2024-02-28","url":"https://www.investing.com/news/economy/embattled-japan-pm-faces-ethics-committee-to-save-popularity-and-budget-3319362","summary":"Kishida had to appear before a parliamentary ethics committee and manage the funding scandal while protecting the budget process. That shows the implementation agenda was reactive and partly consumed by damage control.","question_ids":["8B.2","7B.9"]},{"title":"Reuters: wage gains real, but weak yen and scandals blunted payoff","publisher":"Reuters","date":"2024-08-14","url":"https://www.thestar.com.my/news/world/2024/08/14/analysis-japan039s-kishida-championed-039new-capitalism039-but-was-undone-by-yen","summary":"Reuters said the wage program existed, but external shocks and scandals prevented it from fully landing. This is negative on realized implementation, even though the policy machinery was real.","question_ids":["8B.2"]},{"title":"Reuters: government downgraded economic view after weak data","publisher":"Reuters","date":"2024-02-21","url":"https://www.investing.com/news/economic-indicators/japan-downgrades-view-of-economy-on-sluggish-consumer-spending-3309375","summary":"The downgrade shows Kishida’s administration was responding to weak conditions rather than steadily delivering on the growth plan. It is evidence of fragility in execution, not absence of planning.","question_ids":["8B.2"]},{"title":"AP: legacy of compromise and factional politics","publisher":"Associated Press","date":"2024-09-30","url":"https://apnews.com/article/05926b50f4f5a83a631f779d906cf06d","summary":"AP described Kishida as compromising with powerful conservative nationalists to stay in power. That suggests coalition bargaining diluted programmatic autonomy and likely shaped which priorities were feasible.","question_ids":["8B.2","8B.1"]},{"title":"“Illegal foreigners zero” platform page","publisher":"Kishida Fumio official website / LDP-affiliated site","date":"2024","url":"https://kishida.gr.jp/fact/","summary":"The tougher migration-control agenda shows a concrete enforcement focus, but it is mixed because it looks more like exclusionary control than broad programmatic delivery.","question_ids":["8B.2","7B.9"]}]}
